mainTopic: How far טומאה spreads in a winepress, and how to make utensils bought from a גוי fit for use: טבילה, הגעלה, ליבון, and which utensils need them.
overview: The amud opens by finishing the rules for preparing woven winepress items, then brings a מחלוקת between רבי and רבי חייא about how far טומאה spreads when an עם הארץ touches grapes in a winepress. The גמרא defends the lenient view, saying the grape clusters block the wine, and rules that way in practice. A new משנה teaches that utensils bought from גוים are prepared the way they were used: טבילה, הגעלה, or ליבון. The גמרא adds that all of them also need טבילה in forty סאה, and learns this from the words וְטָהֵר and בְּמֵי נִדָּה, explaining why both words are needed. Next it sets limits. Even new utensils need טבילה, but only meal utensils, only ones that were bought and not borrowed, and only metal ones. Glass is treated like metal, and the הלכה is that glazed clay follows its finished form. A question about collateral utensils stays unresolved. Finally, a ברייתא lists four levels of koshering, two ברייתות disagree about food cooked before koshering, and the גמרא ties this to נותן טעם לפגם. רב חייא בריה דרב הונא begins answering how the Torah's ban still applies, and his answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Finishing the list: how to purify woven items of צבתא and flax
steps.stepSummary: Items woven from צבתא must be cleansed. Items woven from flax must be left unused for a while. Any knots must be untied.
steps.simpleTranslation: Those made of צבתא: cleanse them. Those made of flax: let them sit unused for a while. And if they have knots: untie them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a list that began just before this point, about how to make woven items from a non-Jew's winepress usable again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Different materials need different methods. צבתא is cleansed, while flax is left to sit until it becomes 'old.' Knots must be untied, because wine can stay trapped inside a knot.

keyTerms.meaning: A kind of plant fiber used for weaving
Let them become 'old' by sitting unused

phrases.english: Those of tzavta — one must cleanse them;
those of flax — one must leave them unused for a while;

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי אִית בְּהוּ קִיטְרֵי — שָׁרֵי לְהוּ.
phrases.english: and if they have knots — one must untie them.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּצַבְתָּא — לְנַגְּבָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ruling from the previous page about purifying winepress items.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: צבתא items are cleansed, flax items are left unused for a while, and knots must be untied.

steps.title: An עם הארץ touches grape clusters in a winepress
steps.stepSummary: רבי and רבי חייא argue. One says only the touched cluster and its surroundings become טמא. The other says the whole winepress becomes טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: if an עם הארץ reached his hand into a winepress and touched grape clusters, רבי and רבי חייא disagree. One says the cluster and everything around it are טמא, but the rest of the winepress is טהור. The other says the whole winepress is also טמא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It presents a מחלוקת about how far טומאה spreads inside a winepress.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עם הארץ is assumed to be טמא, so his touch makes the cluster טמא. The question is whether the wine connects the whole winepress, so that everything becomes טמא. The text does not tell us which of the two Sages holds which view.

keyTerms.meaning: A person who is not careful about טהרה laws

steps.confusionAlert: 'חַד אָמַר... וְחַד אָמַר' means 'one said... and one said.' The גמרא does not tell us whether רבי or רבי חייא holds each view.

phrases.aramaic: אִיתְּמַר: עַם הָאָרֶץ שֶׁהוֹשִׁיט יָדוֹ לַגַּת
phrases.english: It was stated: an am ha'aretz who reached his hand into the winepress
and touched grape clusters,
Rabbi and Rabbi Chiya disagree:

phrases.aramaic: חַד אָמַר: אֶשְׁכּוֹל וְכׇל סְבִיבוֹתָיו טְמֵאִין,
phrases.english: one says: the cluster and all its surroundings are impure,
but the rest of the whole winepress is pure;

phrases.aramaic: וְחַד אָמַר: כׇּל הַגַּת כּוּלָּהּ נָמֵי טְמֵאָה.
phrases.english: and one says: the whole winepress is also impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר: עַם הָאָרֶץ שֶׁהוֹשִׁיט יָדוֹ לַגַּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic about winepresses, this time about טומאה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Dispute: either only the cluster and its surroundings are טמא, or the entire winepress is טמא.

steps.title: Challenge from the case of a שרץ in a press
steps.stepSummary: The lenient view seems to contradict a משנה: a שרץ in a press makes only its spot טמא, but if liquid is flowing, everything is טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the one who says only the cluster and its surroundings are טמא and the rest of the winepress is טהור, how is this different from the משנה? A שרץ found in a press makes only the place it touches טמא, but if liquid was flowing, everything is טמא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the lenient view using a משנה about a שרץ in a press.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In that משנה, flowing liquid connects the whole press, so everything becomes טמא. A winepress also has wine in it. So why shouldn't the wine connect the whole winepress, making all of it טמא?

keyTerms.meaning: A dead creeping creature, which makes things טמא

phrases.english: And according to the one who says:
the cluster and all its surroundings are impure,
but the rest of the whole winepress is pure,
how is it different from what we learned in a mishna:
a sheretz that was found in a press
makes impure only the place it touches,
but if liquid was flowing —
everything is impure?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְמַאן דְּאָמַר אֶשְׁכּוֹל וְכׇל סְבִיבוֹתָיו טְמֵאִים וְכׇל הַגַּת כּוּלָּהּ טְהוֹרָה מַאי שְׁנָא מֵהָא דִּתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the lenient view from Step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that only the cluster and its surroundings are טמא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה shows that flowing liquid connects everything, so the wine in a winepress should connect all of it as well.

steps.title: The grape clusters block the flow
steps.stepSummary: In the press, nothing interrupts the liquid. In a winepress, the grape clusters interrupt the wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, nothing interrupts the liquid. Here, the grape clusters interrupt it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by pointing out a physical difference between the two cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Liquid spreads טומאה only when it forms one continuous connection. In a winepress, the clusters break the wine into separate parts, so the טומאה stays near the cluster that was touched. The lenient view stands.

keyTerms.meaning: There / here: the classic way to contrast two cases

steps.whatToRemember: Liquid connects things for טומאה only when it flows without interruption. Grape clusters in a winepress break up that connection.

phrases.english: There, nothing at all interrupts,
here, the clusters interrupt.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם לָא מַפְסֵק וְלָא מִידֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 3.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The wine in a winepress connects everything, just like the flowing liquid in the press.
steps.terutzMaskana: The clusters interrupt the wine, so there is no continuous connection and the rest of the winepress stays טהור.

steps.title: The final ruling on the winepress
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן ruled for רבי ירמיה (or his son) like the lenient view: only the cluster and its surroundings are טמא, and the rest of the winepress stays טהור.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן ruled for רבי ירמיה (some say for his son) like the opinion that the cluster and everything around it is טמא, but the rest of the winepress is טהור.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the winepress discussion with a practical ruling. It follows the lenient opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 2, רבי and רבי חייא argued about how far the טומאה spreads. In Step 4 the lenient view was defended, because the grape clusters interrupt the wine. Now we learn that this lenient view is the one followed in practice.

keyTerms.meaning: They ruled, gave a practical instruction
Its surroundings, the area around it

steps.whatToRemember: The final ruling: only the touched cluster and the area around it become טמא. The rest of the גת stays טהור.

phrases.english: The Sages gave a ruling to Rabbi Yirmeya,
and some say, to the son of Rabbi Yirmeya,
in line with the words of the one who says:
The cluster and all its surroundings are impure,
phrases.notes: This is the lenient opinion from Step 2, the one defended in Step 4.

phrases.english: but the entire winepress is pure.

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹרוֹ לֵיהּ רַבָּנַן לְרַבִּי יִרְמְיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the practical ruling after the lenient view was defended in Step 4.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The halacha follows the view that only the cluster and its surroundings are טמא.

steps.title: How to prepare utensils bought from gentiles
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: utensils bought from גוים are cleaned the way they were used. Some get טבילה, some get הגעלה, and some get ליבון. A spit and a grill need ליבון, and a knife only needs polishing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Someone who buys used utensils from gentiles prepares each one the way it is normally used. If it only needs immersion, he immerses it. If it needs boiling water, he purges it in boiling water. If it needs fire, he heats it in fire until it glows. A spit and a grill are heated until they glow. A knife is polished, and then it is fine.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens a new topic. It explains how to make used utensils from גוים fit for use.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is that the cleaning matches how the utensil was used. A utensil used on fire needs fire. A utensil used with boiling liquid needs boiling water. A knife is an easier case, because only its surface needs to be cleaned.

keyTerms.meaning: To heat in fire until glowing hot (ליבון)

steps.confusionAlert: In this משנה, the word טְהוֹרָה means the knife is now fit to use for food. It is not talking about the usual laws of טומאה.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנִי׳ הַלּוֹקֵחַ כְּלֵי תַּשְׁמִישׁ מִן הַגּוֹיִם,
phrases.english: MISHNA: One who buys utensils from the gentiles:
one whose way is to be immersed, he must immerse it;
one whose way is to be purged in boiling water, he must purge it;
one whose way is to be heated white-hot in fire, he must heat it white-hot in fire.
The spit and the grill: he heats them white-hot in fire.
The knife: he polishes it, and it is pure.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַלּוֹקֵחַ כְּלֵי תַּשְׁמִישׁ מִן הַגּוֹיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the winepress ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A utensil bought from a גוי is cleaned the way it was used: טבילה, הגעלה, or ליבון. A knife needs only polishing.

steps.title: All the utensils also need immersion
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא adds that every one of these utensils also needs טבילה in a מקוה of forty סאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: all of them need טבילה in forty סאה of water.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that adds a rule to the משנה. Even after הגעלה or ליבון, the utensil still needs טבילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: From the משנה alone, we might think that boiling or heating is all that is needed. The ברייתא says no: טבילה is always needed as well. A kosher מקוה must have forty סאה of water.

keyTerms.meaning: Forty סאה, the minimum amount of water for a kosher מקוה

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the practice of טבילת כלים on top of הגעלה or ליבון.

phrases.english: GEMARA: It was taught:
And all of them require immersion in forty se'ah.
phrases.notes: "All of them" means even the utensils that already had boiling water or fire.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא: וְכוּלָּן צְרִיכִין טְבִילָה בְּאַרְבָּעִים סְאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a rule to the משנה: טבילה is needed in every case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Every utensil bought from a גוי needs טבילה in forty סאה.

steps.title: Where do we learn this from?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of the טבילה requirement.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of the rule. This question sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gave the rule but did not say where it comes from. The גמרא wants to know which פסוק teaches it.

keyTerms.meaning: From where are these words learned?

phrases.english: From where are these matters derived?

steps.triggerLanguage: מְנָהָנֵי מִילֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the ברייתא's rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which פסוק teaches that the utensils also need טבילה?

steps.title: רבא: the word "and it shall be pure" adds immersion
steps.stepSummary: רבא learns it from the פסוק "pass it through fire, and it shall be pure." The extra word וְטָהֵר adds another purification on top of the fire.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא says: the verse says, "Anything that goes into fire, you shall pass through fire, and it shall be pure." The verse added another purification for you.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question by pointing to a פסוק about the utensils taken from מדין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק has already said to pass the utensil through fire. Then it adds וְטָהֵר, "and it shall be pure." רבא reads this as one more step after the fire, which is טבילה.

keyTerms.meaning: You shall pass it through fire

phrases.english: Rava said: Because the verse says:
"Anything that goes into the fire
you shall pass through the fire, and it shall be pure,"
the verse added for you another purification.
phrases.notes: He means: after the fire, there is one more step, the טבילה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא, דְּאָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra word וְטָהֵר teaches a purification beyond fire, which is טבילה.

steps.title: בר קפרא: "מי נדה", but no sprinkling
steps.stepSummary: בר קפרא looks at the words "במי נדה" in the same passage. These words might suggest sprinkling on the third and seventh days, like טומאת מת. The word אַךְ comes to exclude that.
steps.simpleTranslation: בר קפרא taught: since the פסוק says "with the water of נדה," I might think the utensil needs sprinkling on the third and seventh days. So the פסוק says אַךְ, "nevertheless," which separates this case.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another teaching on the same passage. It shows that the purification water here does not mean sprinkling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words "במי נדה" could make us think of the sprinkling done for טומאת מת on days three and seven. The word אַךְ cuts that off. So the purification with water here is not sprinkling, which fits the טבילה rule.

keyTerms.meaning: The purification water named in the פסוק
"Nevertheless", a word that limits or excludes

phrases.english: Bar Kappara taught:
Since it is stated "with the water of nidda,"
phrases.notes: This comes from the same פסוק, במדבר 31:23.

phrases.aramaic: שׁוֹמֵעַ אֲנִי שֶׁצָּרִיךְ הַזָּאָה שְׁלִישִׁי וּשְׁבִיעִי,
phrases.english: I would understand that it requires sprinkling on the third and seventh days,
therefore the verse says "nevertheless": it made a distinction.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי בַּר קַפָּרָא: מִתּוֹךְ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בְּמֵי נִדָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings another reading of the same passage, from בר קפרא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The words "במי נדה" point to purification with water, and the word אַךְ shows that third-day and seventh-day sprinkling is not needed.

steps.title: Water a נדה immerses in means forty סאה
steps.stepSummary: בר קפרא finishes his reading. Since 'במי נדה' cannot mean sprinkling, it must mean the water a נדה immerses in, which is a forty-סאה מקוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why does the פסוק say 'with the water of נדה'? It means water that a נדה woman immerses in, so you must say forty סאה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes בר קפרא's proof from step 10. The words 'במי נדה' teach that the utensils need a full מקוה of forty סאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 10, the word אַךְ ruled out reading 'נדה' as sprinkling on days three and seven. So the word 'נדה' must point somewhere else: to a woman who is a נדה. She becomes טהור by immersing in forty סאה, so the utensils need the same amount.

keyTerms.meaning: What does the פסוק come to teach?
Here it means a woman in her niddah state, who immerses in a מקוה
You must therefore say (the only option left)
Forty סאה, the minimum amount of water for a kosher מקוה

steps.confusionAlert: The word נדה here does NOT mean the sprinkling water of the פרה אדומה. That reading was just ruled out. It means a woman who is a נדה, and so it points to the water she immerses in.

phrases.aramaic: אִם כֵּן, מָה תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר ״בְּמֵי נִדָּה״?
phrases.english: If so, what does the verse teach by saying "with the water of נדה"?
phrases.notes: 'If so' means: since אַךְ already ruled out sprinkling. במדבר 31:23.

phrases.english: Water in which a נדה woman immerses,
you must say: forty סאה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן, מָה תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes בר קפרא's derivation that began in step 10
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source for forty סאה is 'במי נדה', meaning water fit for a נדה to immerse in

steps.title: Why 'וטהר' alone would not be enough
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that both phrases are needed. If the Torah wrote only 'וטהר', we would think any amount of water works, so it added 'במי נדה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Torah needed to write 'and it shall be pure', and it needed to write 'with the water of נדה'. If it wrote only 'and it shall be pure', I would say any amount of water is enough. So the Torah wrote 'with the water of נדה'.
steps.whatsHappening: Now that we have two sources (רבא's 'וטהר' and בר קפרא's 'במי נדה'), the גמרא explains why the Torah needs both. This step gives the first half of that explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'וטהר' only tells us that some extra purifying is needed. It does not say how much water. 'במי נדה' adds the exact amount, forty סאה.

keyTerms.meaning: I would have thought (the mistaken first idea)
The Merciful One, meaning ה׳ in the Torah

phrases.english: It was necessary to write "and it shall be pure,"
and it was necessary to write "with the water of נדה."
If it had written only "and it shall be pure,"
I would have said: "and it shall be pure" with any amount of water,
so the Merciful One wrote "with the water of נדה."

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיצְטְרִיךְ לְמִיכְתַּב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why both derivations (steps 9 and 11) are needed, starting with the need for 'במי נדה'
steps.terutzHavaAmina: With only 'וטהר', any small amount of water would be enough
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'במי נדה' is needed to set the amount at forty סאה

steps.title: Why 'במי נדה' alone would not be enough
steps.stepSummary: If the Torah wrote only 'במי נדה', we would think the utensil must wait for sunset like a נדה. So 'וטהר' teaches that it is pure right away.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the Torah wrote only 'with the water of נדה', I would say the utensil needs sunset like a נדה. So the Torah wrote 'and it shall be pure', meaning immediately.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the second half of the explanation. 'וטהר' teaches that the utensil becomes usable right after טבילה, with no waiting for sunset.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Comparing the utensil to a נדה might lead us to copy all her rules, including waiting until sunset. 'וטהר' cuts that off: it is pure now. Together the two phrases give the full rule: forty סאה, and usable at once.

keyTerms.meaning: Waiting for sunset before becoming טהור

steps.whatToRemember: Two phrases, two lessons. 'במי נדה' means a forty-סאה מקוה. 'וטהר' means the utensil is usable right after immersing, with no sunset needed.

phrases.english: And if the Merciful One had written only "with the water of נדה,"
I would have said it needs sunset, like a נדה,
so the Merciful One wrote "and it shall be pure": immediately.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי כְּתַב רַחֲמָנָא בְּמֵי נִדָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second half of the explanation from step 12
steps.terutzHavaAmina: With only 'במי נדה', the utensil would need sunset like a נדה
steps.terutzMaskana: 'וטהר' teaches that it is pure immediately
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'וטהר' is needed to teach that the utensil is pure right away

steps.title: Even new utensils need טבילה
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן in the name of רבה בר אבוה rules that even new utensils from a גוי need טבילה. The proof: old utensils after ליבון are like new, and they still need טבילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: even new utensils are included. Old utensils that were made white-hot are just like new ones, and even so they need טבילה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new ruling begins. רב נחמן says טבילה applies even to utensils from a גוי that were never used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After ליבון, an old utensil has no forbidden taste left, so it is like a new one. Yet the ברייתא in step 7 still requires טבילה for it. That shows טבילה is not about removing taste, so new utensils need it too.

keyTerms.meaning: New utensils that were never used
Included in the meaning of the פסוק

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basis for the practical rule that new utensils bought from a גוי need טבילת כלים.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ:
phrases.english: רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה:
Even new utensils are included,
for old ones that one heated white-hot
are like new ones,
and even so they need טבילה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the source of טבילה to which utensils it covers
steps.mimraCoreRuling: New utensils bought from a גוי also need טבילה

steps.title: Then even clothing scissors should need טבילה
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת objects. If even new, unused utensils need טבילה, then clothing scissors bought from a גוי should need it too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת objected: if so, even scissors for clothing should need it too!
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת attacks רב נחמן's ruling by showing where it seems to lead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If טבילה has nothing to do with food taste, why stop at food utensils? Then any metal utensil, even tailor's scissors, would need it. רב ששת treats that result as clearly wrong.

phrases.english: רב ששת objected to it:

phrases.aramaic: אִי הָכִי, אֲפִילּוּ זוּזָא דְּסַרְבָּלָא נָמֵי!
phrases.english: If so, even scissors for clothing should need it too!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב שֵׁשֶׁת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling of step 14
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's rule that even new utensils need טבילה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If טבילה is not tied to forbidden taste, then it should apply to any utensil, even non-food scissors

steps.title: Only meal utensils are in the פרשה
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the Torah's פרשה only talks about utensils used for meals, so only those need טבילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: the פרשה speaks about utensils for meals.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers רב ששת by limiting the law to food utensils.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule does come from the פרשה of the spoils of מדין, and that פרשה deals with cooking and eating utensils. So new food utensils need טבילה, but clothing scissors do not.

keyTerms.meaning: Utensils used for meals (cooking and eating)

steps.whatToRemember: טבילת כלים applies even to new utensils from a גוי, but only to כלי סעודה, utensils used for food.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: כְּלֵי סְעוּדָה אֲמוּרִין בַּפָּרָשָׁה.
phrases.english: He said to him: utensils for meals are what is mentioned in the passage.
phrases.notes: The passage is the spoils of מדין in במדבר 31, which talks about pots and cooking tools.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: כְּלֵי סְעוּדָה אֲמוּרִין בַּפָּרָשָׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב ששת's challenge in step 15
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the scope of the rule to the type of utensils in the source passage
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב ששת thought the ruling would cover every utensil, even scissors
steps.terutzMaskana: Only meal utensils need טבילה, even when they are new

steps.title: Only bought utensils need immersion, not borrowed ones
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן in the name of רבה בר אבוה limits טבילת כלים to utensils bought from a גוי. Borrowed utensils do not need it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: this rule applies only to utensils that were bought, like the story in the Torah. Borrowed utensils do not need טבילה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא limits who needs טבילה. Only a Jew who now owns the utensil must immerse it, not one who is just borrowing it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the Torah's story, the utensils from מדין became fully owned by the Jews. So the requirement applies only when the utensil really passes into Jewish ownership, as in a purchase. A borrowed utensil still belongs to the גוי, so it does not need טבילה.

keyTerms.meaning: They taught this only about (a phrase that limits a rule)
The incident that happened (the story in the Torah)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basis for the practical rule that only utensils a Jew owns need טבילה.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman said in the name of Rabba bar Avuh:
They taught this only about purchased utensils,
like the incident that happened,
phrases.notes: This is the story in במדבר פרק לא, where the utensils taken from מדין became the Jews' own.

phrases.english: but borrowed ones do not.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא בִּלְקוּחִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another limit on טבילת כלים, after the earlier limit to meal utensils.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only utensils bought from a גוי need טבילה. Borrowed ones do not.

steps.title: רב יצחק בר יוסף buys an earthenware utensil
steps.stepSummary: רב יצחק בר יוסף bought a utensil made of מרדא from a גוי and planned to immerse it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יצחק בר יוסף bought a utensil made of מרדא from a גוי, and he thought he had to immerse it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story to set up the next step. A rabbi plans to immerse a non-metal utensil.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The utensil is made of earth mixed with dung, not metal. The story raises the question of whether such a utensil needs טבילה at all. The answer comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A utensil made of earth mixed with dung
He thought he should immerse it

phrases.english: Rav Yitzchak bar Yosef
bought a utensil made of marda from a gentile,
phrases.notes: מרדא is earth mixed with dung, so this is a kind of clay utensil, not metal.

phrases.english: and he thought he should immerse it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב יִצְחָק בַּר יוֹסֵף זְבַן מָנָא דְּמַרְדָּא מִגּוֹי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from which kinds of ownership count to which materials count.

steps.title: רבי יעקב: only metal utensils need immersion
steps.stepSummary: רבי יעקב tells רב יצחק בר יוסף that רבי יוחנן personally explained to him that the פרשה speaks only of metal utensils.
steps.simpleTranslation: One of the rabbis, named רבי יעקב, told him: רבי יוחנן himself explained to me that the פרשה speaks about metal utensils.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יעקב tells רב יצחק בר יוסף that his clay utensil does not need טבילה. Only metal utensils do.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק lists only metals: gold, silver, copper, iron, tin and lead. So the requirement covers metal utensils and not earthenware. רבי יעקב stresses that he heard this from רבי יוחנן directly.

keyTerms.meaning: It was explained to me personally

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the basic rule that טבילת כלים applies to metal utensils.

phrases.english: One of the Rabbis said to him,
and Rabbi Yaakov was his name:

phrases.aramaic: לְדִידִי מִפָּרְשָׁא לֵיהּ מִינֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: To me it was explained by Rabbi Yochanan himself:
Metal utensils are what is mentioned in the passage.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ הָהוּא מֵרַבָּנַן וְרַבִּי יַעֲקֹב שְׁמֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the plan from step 18 to immerse a clay utensil.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רב יצחק בר יוסף's assumption that any utensil from a גוי needs טבילה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The פרשה speaks only of metal utensils, so clay ones are not included.

steps.title: Glass utensils are treated like metal
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי rules that glass utensils need טבילה, because like metal they can be melted down and remade when broken.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: glass utensils, since they can be fixed when broken, are like metal utensils.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי adds glass to the list of utensils that need טבילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A broken metal utensil can be melted and made into a new one. Glass works the same way. Because of this shared quality, glass is treated like metal and needs טבילה.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
these glass utensils,

phrases.aramaic: הוֹאִיל וְכִי נִשְׁתַּבְּרוּ יֵשׁ לָהֶן תַּקָּנָה,
phrases.english: since when they break they can be fixed,
they are like metal utensils.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: הָנֵי כְּלֵי זְכוּכִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Widens the metal rule from step 19 to include glass.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Glass utensils need טבילה like metal ones.

steps.title: Dispute over glazed clay utensils
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא and רבינא argue about a clay utensil coated with glaze. One follows its beginning as clay, and the other follows its end as a glazed utensil.
steps.simpleTranslation: About a glazed utensil, רב אחא and רבינא argue. One says we follow its beginning, and one says we follow its end.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a מחלוקת about a mixed case: a clay utensil coated with a glaze.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One view looks at the utensil's start: it is clay, so it needs no טבילה. The other view looks at its finished form: it has a glaze coating, so it needs טבילה.

keyTerms.meaning: A clay utensil coated with glaze

phrases.english: A glazed earthenware utensil,
Rav Acha and Ravina argue about it.
One said: we follow its beginning,
and one said: we follow its end.

steps.triggerLanguage: קוּנְיָא, פְּלִיגִי בַּהּ רַב אַחָא וְרָבִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After setting rules for metal and glass, the גמרא turns to a mixed clay and glaze utensil.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a מחלוקת whether glazed clay follows its clay beginning or its glazed end.

steps.title: The halacha follows the final state
steps.stepSummary: The הלכה follows the utensil's end, so glazed clay utensils need טבילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The הלכה follows its end.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא decides the מחלוקת: glazed clay utensils need טבילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We judge the utensil by its finished form, with the glaze coating. So it is treated like a metal utensil and must be immersed.
steps.whatToRemember: טבילה applies to metal and glass utensils, and to glazed clay ones, which follow their finished form. Plain earthenware does not need it.

phrases.english: And the halacha follows its end.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהִלְכְתָא כְּסוֹפוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides the מחלוקת in step 21.

steps.title: What about a utensil held as collateral?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether a utensil a Jew holds as collateral from a גוי needs טבילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: what is the law of a utensil held as collateral?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new question. A collateral utensil falls between a bought one and a borrowed one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 17 said bought utensils need טבילה and borrowed ones do not. A pledge stays with the Jew for a while, but it still belongs to the גוי. So it is unclear which side it falls on.

phrases.english: They asked:
A utensil held as collateral, what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: מַשְׁכַּנְתָּא מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the bought versus borrowed rule from step 17 and asks about a case in between.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a collateral utensil count as bought, so it needs טבילה, or as borrowed, so it does not?

steps.title: רב אשי immersed a collateral silver cup
steps.stepSummary: מר בר רב אשי reports that his father רב אשי held a silver cup as collateral from a גוי, immersed it, and drank from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר בר רב אשי said: a גוי gave my father a silver cup as collateral, and he immersed it and drank from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a story that seems to answer the question: רב אשי immersed a collateral utensil.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It looks like proof that collateral is treated like a bought utensil. But the next step shows the reason for his action is unclear.

phrases.english: Mar bar Rav Ashi said:

phrases.aramaic: אַבָּא מַשְׁכֵּן לֵיהּ גּוֹי כָּסָא דְּכַסְפָּא,
phrases.english: A gentile gave my father a silver cup as collateral,
and he immersed it and drank from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר בַּר רַב אָשֵׁי: אַבָּא מַשְׁכֵּן לֵיהּ גּוֹי כָּסָא דְּכַסְפָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a real-life case to answer the question in step 23.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב אשי immersed a collateral cup, which suggests it needs טבילה.

steps.title: The reason for immersing is unclear
steps.stepSummary: מר בר רב אשי admits he does not know why his father immersed the cup. Either collateral counts as a purchase, or the גוי clearly meant to leave the cup with him for good.
steps.simpleTranslation: But I don't know whether he did it because he held that collateral is like a purchase, or because he saw that the גוי planned to leave the cup with him.
steps.whatsHappening: מר בר רב אשי weakens his own proof. His father's action could have a different reason, so the question is not settled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If collateral is like a purchase, every collateral utensil needs טבילה. But maybe רב אשי saw that this גוי would never redeem the cup, so it was effectively his. With two possible reasons, the story does not decide the general question.

keyTerms.meaning: To leave it with him for good

steps.whatToRemember: The question of collateral stays open. רב אשי did immerse such a cup, but it may only be because the גוי planned to abandon it.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not take רב אשי's action as a clear ruling that collateral always needs טבילה. His own son says the reason is unknown.

phrases.english: But I do not know
whether it was because he held
that collateral is like a purchase,
or because he saw about the gentile
that his intention was to leave it with him.
phrases.notes: Literally, "to sink it." The גוי planned never to come back and redeem the cup.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא יָדַעְנָא אִי מִשּׁוּם דְקָסָבַר מַשְׁכַּנְתָּא כִּזְבִינֵי דָּמְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Undercuts the proof from step 24 by offering another explanation.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Using רב אשי's action as proof that collateral counts as a purchase
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: He may have immersed the cup only because this גוי meant to abandon it, which makes it like the Jew's own.

steps.title: Four levels of preparing utensils bought from a גוי
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches how to prepare utensils bought from a גוי, based on how the גוי used them: not at all, with cold, with hot, or directly on fire.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: Someone who buys utensils from גוים: if the items were never used, he immerses them and they are pure. If they were used with cold things, like cups, jugs and flasks, he rinses them, immerses them, and they are pure. If they were used with hot things, like pots, kettles and water-heaters, he purges them in boiling water, immerses them, and they are pure. If they were used directly on fire, like spits and grills, he heats them until they glow, immerses them, and they are pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that lays out the basic rules for preparing a utensil bought from a גוי. The method depends on how the utensil was used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every utensil needs טבילה. On top of that, the more strongly the forbidden food went into the utensil, the stronger the cleaning: rinsing for cold, boiling water (הגעלה) for hot, and fire (ליבון) for direct heat. The rule is that a utensil is cleaned the same way it absorbed the food.

keyTerms.meaning: He purges them in boiling water (הגעלה)
He heats them in fire until they glow (ליבון)

steps.whatToRemember: Every utensil from a גוי needs טבילה. Used utensils also need cleaning that matches how they were used: cold means rinsing, hot means הגעלה, and fire means ליבון.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא is the classic source for the practical rules of koshering utensils.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
One who buys food utensils from the gentiles,
items that were not used
he immerses them, and they are pure.

phrases.aramaic: דְּבָרִים שֶׁנִּשְׁתַּמֵּשׁ בָּהֶן עַל יְדֵי צוֹנֵן,
phrases.english: Items that were used with cold things,
such as cups, jugs, and flasks
he rinses them, immerses them, and they are pure.

phrases.aramaic: דְּבָרִים שֶׁנִּשְׁתַּמֵּשׁ בָּהֶן עַל יְדֵי חַמִּין,
phrases.english: Items that were used with hot things,
such as large pots, kettles, and water-heaters
he purges them, immerses them, and they are pure.
phrases.notes: "Purges" means putting them into boiling water so the absorbed taste comes out.

phrases.aramaic: דְּבָרִים שֶׁנִּשְׁתַּמֵּשׁ בָּהֶן עַל יְדֵי הָאוּר,
phrases.english: Items that were used directly with fire,
such as spits and grills
he heats them until white-hot, immerses them, and they are pure.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הַלּוֹקֵחַ כְּלֵי תַּשְׁמִישׁ מִן הַגּוֹיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the question of which utensils need טבילה to a full ברייתא about how to prepare utensils bought from a גוי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A utensil bought from a גוי always needs טבילה. A used one also needs cleaning that matches its use: rinsing, הגעלה, or ליבון.

steps.title: Two ברייתות disagree about food cooked before koshering
steps.stepSummary: If someone cooked in these utensils before immersing or koshering them, one ברייתא says the food is forbidden and another says it is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: And for all of these utensils, if someone used them before immersing, purging, or heating them until white-hot, one ברייתא teaches that the food is forbidden, and another ברייתא teaches that it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that two ברייתות contradict each other about food cooked in a גוי's utensils before they were made kosher. This sets up the next step, where the גמרא will resolve the contradiction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both ברייתות agree that the utensil should be koshered first. The question is only what happens after the fact: is the food that was already cooked in it forbidden or permitted?
steps.confusionAlert: "Forbidden" and "permitted" here are about the food cooked in the utensil, not the utensil itself. Everyone agrees the utensil still needs koshering.

phrases.english: And all of them that one used
before he immersed them
and before he purged them and before he heated them white-hot,
one ברייתא teaches: forbidden,
phrases.notes: He means the food that was cooked in the utensil.

phrases.english: and another ברייתא teaches: permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי חֲדָא: אָסוּר, וְתַנְיָא אִידַּךְ: מוּתָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the ברייתא's koshering rules and asks about food cooked in the utensils before they were koshered, where two sources contradict each other.
steps.kashyaTarget: The status of food cooked in a גוי's utensils before koshering
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two ברייתות give opposite rulings on the same case, so they cannot both be right as they stand.

steps.title: Each ברייתא follows a different view on a bad-tasting flavor
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא resolves the contradiction: the strict ברייתא holds that a flavor which spoils the food still forbids it, and the lenient ברייתא holds that such a flavor does not forbid it.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. This ברייתא follows the one who says that a forbidden flavor which spoils the food still makes it forbidden. That ברייתא follows the one who says that a forbidden flavor which spoils the food leaves it permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by saying the two ברייתות follow two sides of a known מחלוקת about נותן טעם לפגם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A taste left over in a used pot makes the new food taste worse. The ברייתא that forbids the food holds that even a spoiling taste forbids it. The ברייתא that permits the food holds that a spoiling taste does not forbid it.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; the contradiction can be resolved
A forbidden substance that gives a bad, spoiling taste to permitted food

phrases.english: It is not difficult.
This one follows the one who says:
a substance that imparts a spoiling flavor makes it forbidden,
and that one follows the one who says:
a substance that imparts a spoiling flavor leaves it permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא, הָא כְּמַאן דְּאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction from step 27 by assigning each ברייתא to a different view.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning each source to a different side of a known מחלוקת (נותן טעם לפגם)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two ברייתות seemed to contradict each other with no explanation.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each ברייתא follows a different opinion about whether a spoiling flavor forbids food.

steps.title: Why does the Torah require koshering if a spoiling taste is permitted?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the lenient view: if a spoiling flavor is permitted, how can there ever be a case where the Torah's ban on unkoshered utensils of a גוי applies?
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to the one who says that a spoiling flavor is permitted, the utensils of גוים that need purging, which the Torah forbade, how can you ever find that case?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the lenient opinion from step 28. The Torah clearly requires purging a גוי's utensils, but under this view it seems there would be no reason to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A used pot's leftover taste always spoils new food. If a spoiling taste is permitted, then food cooked in an unkoshered pot should always be fine, and the Torah's command to purge would never matter. The גמרא asks how the lenient view explains the Torah's command.

keyTerms.meaning: Utensils of גוים that need purging in boiling water
How can you find such a case?

steps.whyThisMatters: This challenge threatens the whole lenient view of נותן טעם לפגם, because that view seems to leave the Torah's koshering command with no purpose.

phrases.english: But according to the one who says:
a substance that imparts a spoiling flavor is permitted,
the gentiles' utensils that need purging, which the Merciful One forbade,
phrases.notes: This refers to the utensils taken from מדין, which the Torah says must be koshered (במדבר 31:23).

phrases.english: how can you find such a case?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְמַאן דְּאָמַר: נוֹתֵן טַעַם לִפְגָם — מוּתָּר, גִּיעוּלֵי גוֹיִם דְּאָסַר רַחֲמָנָא הֵיכִי מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the lenient view used in step 28 and challenges it from the Torah's command to purge a גוי's utensils.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that נותן טעם לפגם is permitted
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A used utensil's taste always spoils food. If a spoiling taste is permitted, the Torah's command to purge such utensils would never have any practical effect.

steps.title: The Torah only forbade a pot
steps.stepSummary: רב חייא בריה דרב הונא begins answering the challenge from step 29 by saying the Torah's ban covers only a pot.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חייא, the son of רב הונא, says: The Torah forbade nothing except a pot.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רב חייא בריה דרב הונא to answer the question from step 29. He starts by saying the Torah's ban on a גוי's utensils is limited to a pot, and he will describe exactly which kind of pot right after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 29 asked: if a spoiling flavor does not forbid food, when would the Torah's ban ever apply? רב חייא answers by narrowing the ban. The Torah did not forbid every utensil in every situation, only one particular case of a pot. This opens the way to a case where the flavor is not spoiled, so the Torah's ban still has real meaning.

keyTerms.meaning: The Torah forbade, meaning a ban that comes from the Torah itself
Not... except; a phrase that limits a rule to one case only

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רב חייא means that only pots ever need koshering. He is answering one narrow question: in what case does the Torah's own ban apply, given the view that a spoiling flavor is permitted.
steps.whyThisMatters: This saves the lenient ברייתא from step 28. It shows that a person can hold that a spoiling flavor is permitted and still have a real case where the Torah's ban on a גוי's utensils applies.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: Rav Ḥiyya, son of Rav Huna, says:
The Torah forbade only a pot

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא אָסְרָה תּוֹרָה אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the קשיא of step 29 by limiting the Torah's ban to a specific case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope: the Torah's ban is narrowed to one particular case (a pot), so it is not left with no use.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If a spoiling flavor is permitted, the Torah's ban on a גוי's unkoshered utensils would seem to have no case at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: The Torah's ban applies only to a specific pot case, which will be shown not to involve a spoiling flavor, so the ban is still meaningful.
